description:
Welcome to ASTRONEXA. We are young space enthusiasts and junior innovators in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We connect curiosity, creativity, space science through storytelling, interactive learning & NASA open data. Together, we aim to explore "The Next Frontier" with teamwork and fresh ideas.

Tagline: Connecting Today’s Ideas with Tomorrow’s Discoveries.
summary: ASTRONEXA Mission Academy is an interactive, 100% offline Martian Outpost Trainer built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer"). Designed for elementary and middle-school cadets, the simulator transforms complex space science into hands-on flight-director training. Powered by real NASA InSight Sol 500 telemetry, NASA DONKI space weather records, and NASA Fission Surface Power (FSP) & Human Research Program (HRP) baselines, cadets evaluate Earth vs. Space engineering trade-offs, balance a strict 100 kW continuous nuclear fission power grid, and survive a real S2 solar proton storm (50 kW emergency reserve). Built in clean HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript with zero external dependencies and full English–Bengali bilingual support, ASTRONEXA runs smoothly on any classroom computer without internet access and awards each successful cadet an official Mission Diploma.
details:
OVERVIEW & CHALLENGE ADDRESSED

Young learners often find space science abstract when taught only through textbooks. ASTRONEXA Mission Academy solves this by placing students in the role of a Junior Flight Director managing a deep-space habitat on Mars. Directly addressing the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, it turns real NASA mission data into an interactive, classroom-ready simulation.

HOW IT WORKS (3 ENGINEERING MODULES)

1. Outpost Architecture Setup: Cadets evaluate Earth vs. Space technologies and deploy three NASA-verified subsystems: Sintered Regolith Radiation Shielding, Closed-Loop Hydroponic Bays, and a NASA Fission Surface Power (FSP) Reactor, receiving immediate engineering feedback when selecting unviable Earth-based alternatives.

2. Live 100 kW Power Grid & Life Support Balancing: Using NASA InSight Mars Lander Sol 500 environmental telemetry (-63°C surface temperature, ~720 Pa pressure, 590 W/m² solar insolation), cadets manage real-time energy allocation across life support, thermal heating, hydroponics, and science labs without exceeding the 100 kW reactor cap.

3. S2 Solar Proton Storm Crisis Simulation: Modeled on NASA DONKI Solar Energetic Particle records (Event #2024-05-11T02:00:00-SEP-001), an incoming radiation storm forces cadets to drop power consumption to a strict 50 kW emergency battery reserve while keeping crew radiation exposure safe. Upon completing all three modules, cadets generate a downloadable Mission Diploma.

TECHNICAL STACK, ACCESSIBILITY & IMPACT

Built entirely with semantic HTML5, modern CSS3, and modular Vanilla JavaScript, the simulator requires zero internet connectivity, zero external libraries, and minimal hardware—making it ideal for rural or low-bandwidth schools. Full English and Bengali bilingual support ensures inclusive STEM education for young learners worldwide.
